Nephrotic Syndrome
Deﬁ nition
Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is an abnormal condition that is 
marked by a deﬁ ciency of albumin in the blood and its excre-
tion in the urine due to altered permeability of the glomerular 
basement membranes.
Epidemiology
About two in every 10,000 people experience nephrotic syn-
drome. Th e prevalence is diﬃ  cult to establish in adults because
the condition is usually a result of an underlying disease. Ne-
phrotic syndrome may occur at any age but is more prevalent in
children than in adults. In children, it is most common between
the ages 1½ and 4 years, and aﬀ ects more males than females.
